excerpt: Automations let Perplexity Computer run recurring work on a schedule or on Slack, Gmail, Outlook, Linear and GitHub triggers. Plans, credits, alternatives.
content:
Automations is a feature of Perplexity Computer, Perplexity's agent that carries out tasks rather than only answering questions. An automation is a standing assignment: you describe a job once, and Computer runs it on a schedule or when something happens in Slack, Gmail, Outlook, Linear or GitHub. Conditions, such as a message from a particular sender, narrow which events start a run. Each run can see what earlier runs did, so a weekly competitor price check compares against last week's figures instead of starting from scratch.

You create one by describing it in Computer's prompt box or by choosing New Automation, then adding instructions, a trigger, the connected accounts and Projects it may use, and where the output should go. You decide which actions Computer may take alone and which need your review first, for example before it posts an update in Slack. The dashboard shows each automation's status and run history, including what triggered a run and what it produced, and lets you edit or pause it. Automations replace Perplexity's earlier Scheduled Tasks, which can be migrated.

Perplexity announced Automations on its blog on 29 September 2026. It was posted to Product Hunt under the Perplexity product page by hunter Rohan Chaubey and finished #3 for the day on 11 October 2026, with 193 upvotes and 3 comments.

We have not tested Automations in Perplexity Computer ourselves. This page brings together Perplexity's announcement, help center and pricing pages, the Product Hunt launch and the official pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

paragraphs: Rohan Chaubey, who hunted the launch, described Automations as a way to turn recurring work into long-running agents that run on schedules or triggers and keep context over time, instead of treating every task as a fresh request.

He listed monitoring Slack, Gmail, Outlook, Linear and GitHub, drafting customer replies, finding missed updates, comparing competitor pricing, updating project decisions and sending work for human review. He said it is aimed at Computer users who manage ongoing work across projects and connected tools.
launch_story.attribution: Rohan Chaubey, hunter, on Product Hunt

use_cases: A weekly comparison of competitor prices that updates a spreadsheet and notes what changed since last time
Drafting customer replies in Gmail for a person to review before sending
Watching a Slack channel for cancellations or blocked deals and writing a risk report
Keeping a decision log up to date when a decision is posted in Slack
Opening a pull request when a Linear issue is labelled ready
Flagging missed updates or passed deadlines across projects

fit: already pay for Perplexity and want recurring research or follow-ups to run without a prompt each time
run work across Slack, Gmail, Outlook, Linear or GitHub and want an agent to react to events there
want a human-review step before an agent sends or posts anything
not_fit: are on the free Perplexity plan: Computer needs an active subscription
need predictable fixed costs: each run spends credits, and cost varies with how complex the task is
need precise, rule-based automations across many apps, where a dedicated workflow tool may suit better

pricing.intro: Automations are part of Perplexity Computer, which needs a paid Perplexity subscription; Perplexity says any Computer user can use Automations. Watching for a trigger is free, and credits are spent only when a run executes. Prices are Perplexity's, in US dollars.

plans.name: Pro
plans.detail: Computer access with a weekly allowance of Computer usage, no monthly credit pool, and a one-time 4,000-credit bonus for new subscribers that expires after about 30 days

plans.name: Max
plans.detail: 10,000 Computer credits a month plus a one-time 35,000-credit bonus; default monthly spending cap of $200, adjustable up to $5,000. Brain, the memory system for Computer, is in preview for Max subscribers

notes: Perplexity prices extra credits at 100 credits for $1. Auto-refill is off by default; when switched on it tops up below 500 credits on Pro or 2,500 on Max.
If credits run out, active tasks pause rather than cancel. The older Scheduled Tasks guide says a skipped run can leave a task paused until you re-enable it.
Enterprise Pro starts at $40 a seat a month or $400 a year, per Perplexity's help center; Computer for Enterprise has its own help page.

pros: Runs on events in Slack, Gmail, Outlook, Linear and GitHub as well as on a schedule
Each run builds on earlier runs instead of starting fresh
You choose which actions need your review before they happen
No credits are used while an automation is waiting for its trigger
Run history shows what triggered each run and what it produced
cons: Needs a paid Perplexity plan, and runs spend credits whose cost varies by task
Pro has a weekly usage allowance rather than a monthly credit pool, so heavy use points to the $200 Max plan
Limited to the connectors Perplexity supports for triggers
A run can be skipped if credits run low or a connector's authorisation expires

faq.q: What are Automations in Perplexity Computer?
faq.a: Standing assignments for Perplexity's Computer agent. You describe a job once and it runs on a schedule or when an event happens in Slack, Gmail, Outlook, Linear or GitHub, building on what earlier runs did.

faq.q: Which Perplexity plan do I need?
faq.a: Computer needs an active paid subscription, and Perplexity says any Computer user can use Automations. Pro is $17 a month billed annually with a weekly Computer allowance; Max is $200 a month with 10,000 credits a month.

faq.q: Do automations use credits while they wait?
faq.a: No. Perplexity says no credits are used while Computer watches for a trigger; credits are spent only when a run executes. 100 credits cost $1.

faq.q: Can I change an automation later?
faq.a: Yes. The Automations dashboard lets you edit, pause, run now or delete an automation, and shows each run's trigger and result.

faq.q: Can it act without asking me?
faq.a: Only where you allow it. You choose which actions Computer may take on its own and which need your review, and admins can limit connector permissions.
Automations replace them. Existing Scheduled Tasks appear in the Automations view and can be migrated when you open each one.
Zapier and Lindy are dedicated automation and AI-assistant tools; ChatGPT and Genspark are general AI assistants that Product Hunt lists as Perplexity alternatives.

alternatives.intro: Product Hunt's alternatives for Perplexity as a whole are search and assistant tools; we picked the two closest to agents, ChatGPT and Genspark, and added Zapier and Lindy, which focus on automation. Prices come from each product's own pricing page, checked on 15 October 2026; review scores are Product Hunt users' own.

items.name: Zapier
items.what: No-code automation platform with Zaps and AI Agents
items.starts_at: Free (100 tasks a month); Professional from $19.99/month billed annually
items.difference: Built around explicit trigger-and-action workflows; its Agents have a free allowance of 400 activities a month and are counted separately from tasks.

items.name: Lindy
items.what: AI assistant that works in Slack on inbox, meeting prep and scheduled routines
items.starts_at: $50 of free credits for 7 days; Team $29.99/month per active user
items.difference: Sold as a standalone assistant priced per user, rather than as a feature of an AI search subscription.

items.name: ChatGPT
items.what: Get answers. Find inspiration. Be more productive.
items.difference: A general-purpose assistant for writing, coding and multimodal work; check OpenAI's own pages for its options for recurring work.

items.name: Genspark
items.what: Reinvent Search, the New AI Agent Engine
items.difference: Product Hunt highlights its shareable Sparkpages and no-code multi-agent workflow builder.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Komo, Andi and xdge AI as Perplexity alternatives.
